name: Losar at Ghoom and the Darjeeling monasteries
when: February or early March (Tibetan New Year, first day of the first Tibetan month)
summary: Losar is the Tibetan New Year, kept by Tibetan, Sherpa, Bhutia and Yolmo families across the Darjeeling hills. Monasteries such as Yiga Choeling at Ghoom hang new prayer flags, hold prayers and masked dances, and homes fill with khapse biscuits and visitors.
body: The date follows the Tibetan lunar calendar, so it moves each year, usually falling in February and sometimes in early March. The days before are for cleaning houses and settling debts, and on the eve families eat guthuk, a noodle soup with dough balls hiding small objects that tell your fortune for the year in jest.

In Darjeeling the most visible signs are at the monasteries: Yiga Choeling at Ghoom, Dali monastery near Ghoom and the smaller gompas in town. New prayer flags go up on the ridges, butter lamps burn through the day and monks perform prayers. Some monasteries stage cham, masked dances, around the new year, though dates vary by monastery and lineage.
For visitors Losar is a chance to see the hills in their clear winter light, with cold, bright days and few tourists. Shops in Tibetan neighbourhoods may close for a few days, so stock up beforehand.
tips: Ask your hotel or the monastery office for that year's prayer and dance schedule; dates shift with the lunar calendar
Dress modestly, walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels, and ask before photographing monks
Carry warm layers: February mornings in Ghoom are close to freezing
Expect some Tibetan-run shops and restaurants to close for two or three days

faqs.q: When is Losar celebrated in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Losar starts on the first day of the first month of the Tibetan lunar calendar, which usually falls in February and sometimes in early March. The exact date changes every year. Gyalpo Losar, the version most Tibetan and Sherpa families keep, is the main one in Darjeeling. Check the calendar for your year before you travel and plan two or three days around it.

faqs.q: Can tourists attend Losar prayers at Ghoom Monastery?
faqs.a: Yes, visitors are generally welcome to watch prayers at Yiga Choeling in Ghoom and other monasteries, as long as they are respectful. Stand at the side, keep voices low, do not use flash and ask before photographing monks or rituals. A small offering at the altar is welcome but never required. Rules may vary on major prayer days.

faqs.q: Are there masked dances at Losar in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Some monasteries in and around Darjeeling perform cham, masked dances, near the new year, but schedules vary by monastery and year, and some hold their main dances at other times. Ask locally or phone the monastery office a week ahead. Do not plan a trip around a dance date without confirming it. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What food is eaten at Losar?
faqs.a: On the eve, families eat guthuk, a nine-ingredient noodle soup with dough balls that hide items such as chilli, salt or wool, each with a joking meaning. Over the new year, homes serve khapse, fried twisted biscuits, along with butter tea, momos and meat dishes. Tibetan restaurants in Darjeeling sometimes serve khapse in the weeks around Losar.

name: Dashain and Tihar in the Darjeeling hills
when: Late September to mid-November (Dashain, then Tihar about three weeks later)
summary: Dashain and Tihar are the two largest festivals of Nepali-speaking families in Darjeeling, Kurseong and Mirik. Dashain brings red tika, blessings from elders and bamboo swings; Tihar brings oil lamps, garlands for animals and the singing of deusi and bhailo.
body: Dashain is a fifteen-day festival that ends on Vijaya Dashami, the same day Bengal celebrates the close of Durga Puja. Families gather, and elders place red tika and jamara, young barley shoots, on the foreheads of younger relatives with a blessing. Children play on tall bamboo swings called ping put up in villages. Offices and schools close, and many people travel home.

Tihar follows about three weeks later and lasts five days. Crows, dogs and cows are honoured on successive days with garlands and food, houses are lit with lamps for Laxmi Puja, and groups of young people go door to door singing bhailo and deusi songs in return for gifts. On Bhai Tika, sisters bless their brothers with a seven-coloured tika.
For travellers this is peak season in Darjeeling, with clear October skies and full hotels. It is a good time to see family life, but transport is crowded on the days before and after Dashami.
tips: Book hotels and the toy train joy ride early; October is the busiest month in Darjeeling
Shared jeeps fill fast before and after Dashami as families travel home, so start early
If you are invited to receive tika, accept it with both hands and a small bow
Darjeeling streets are lit with lamps on the night of Laxmi Puja during Tihar

faqs.q: When are Dashain and Tihar in Darjeeling?
faqs.a: Both follow the lunar calendar. Dashain usually falls between late September and mid-October, with Vijaya Dashami as its main tika day. Tihar comes about three weeks later, in late October or November, overlapping with Diwali. Check the dates for your year, because the hills are busiest around these days and transport and hotels fill early.

faqs.q: Is Dashain a good time to visit Darjeeling?
faqs.a: The weather is excellent, with clear skies after the monsoon and good mountain views. The downside is crowds: Bengali families travel for Puja holidays at the same time, so hotels and toy train seats sell out and prices rise by 20–40 percent. Book six to eight weeks ahead, or come in early November once the holiday rush ends.

They are Tihar songs sung door to door. Girls and women traditionally sing bhailo, and boys and men sing deusi, though mixed groups are common today. Households give money, food or sweets in return, and the singers offer blessings for the year. In Darjeeling you may hear groups in the evenings around Laxmi Puja, often with a madal drum.

faqs.q: Will shops and transport close during Dashain?
faqs.a: Government offices, banks and many shops close for several days around Vijaya Dashami, and some drivers take leave. Hotels, restaurants and tourist services keep working, but shared jeeps can be scarce on the main tika day. Withdraw cash before the holiday, book your car in advance and confirm timings. Check current status before you travel.

name: Durga Puja in Siliguri
when: September or October (the five days ending on Vijaya Dashami)
summary: Durga Puja is the biggest festival in Siliguri, the largest city in north Bengal. For five days neighbourhood clubs build pandals, temporary shrines for the goddess, and the city stays out late visiting them.
body: Each neighbourhood committee builds a pandal of bamboo and cloth, often themed and lit with thousands of bulbs, around a clay image of Durga slaying the buffalo demon with her children beside her. The main days are Saptami, Ashtami and Navami, when crowds walk from pandal to pandal late into the night and food stalls sell rolls, phuchka and sweets.

On Vijaya Dashami married women smear vermilion on each other in sindur khela, and the images are carried to the Mahananda river for immersion. In the hills, the same day is the Dashain tika day for Nepali families, so the whole region is on holiday.
If you are passing through Siliguri at Puja time, an evening of pandal-hopping is worth it. Plan for heavy traffic and very busy trains and flights.
tips: Go after 8 pm when the lights are on, but expect large crowds and slow traffic
Book trains and flights to NJP and Bagdogra well ahead; Puja holiday travel is heavy
Wear comfortable shoes; pandal-hopping means a lot of walking

faqs.q: When is Durga Puja in Siliguri?
faqs.a: Durga Puja follows the lunar calendar and usually falls between late September and late October. The main festival days are Shashthi to Vijaya Dashami, five days in all. Check the dates for your year. The busiest nights in Siliguri are Saptami, Ashtami and Navami, when most families go out to visit pandals until late.

faqs.q: Is Durga Puja a problem for travel to Darjeeling?
faqs.a: It can be. Puja holidays send many Bengali families to the hills, so trains to NJP, flights to Bagdogra, hotels and toy train seats sell out. Hill roads also see more traffic. If your dates are fixed, book six to eight weeks ahead. If they are flexible, travelling a week after Vijaya Dashami is calmer and the skies are still clear.

faqs.q: Where are the best pandals in Siliguri?
faqs.a: Large pandals are spread across the city, with many in neighbourhoods off Hill Cart Road, Sevoke Road and around Hakimpara and Subhash Pally. Themes and the most talked-about pandals change each year. Ask your hotel or a local driver which ones are drawing crowds that year, and hire a car for the evening rather than relying on autos.

Sindur khela is a ritual on Vijaya Dashami when married women offer vermilion to the goddess before her immersion and then smear it on each other's faces and hair, wishing each other a long married life. It takes place at pandals before the images leave for the river. Visitors may watch, but ask before photographing anyone.
